proposedTopics.title: Automated Market Makers (AMMs)
proposedTopics.description: How on-chain exchanges price and settle without an orderbook: a bonding curve invariant (constant-product, constant-sum, or stableswap) holds reserves in a pool, and every trade moves along the curve.

proposedTopics.title: Uniswap V2
proposedTopics.description: The canonical constant-product AMM: pair contracts holding two reserves, LP tokens for shares, a cumulative-price TWAP oracle, flash swaps, and an optional protocol fee. The reference every later AMM is measured against.

proposedTopics.title: Uniswap V3
proposedTopics.description: Concentrated liquidity: LPs supply capital only within a chosen price range, expressed via ticks and a sqrtPriceX96 fixed-point price, with per-position fee-growth accounting. Far higher capital efficiency at the cost of active management.

proposedTopics.title: Uniswap V4
proposedTopics.description: A singleton PoolManager holding all pools, flash accounting via transient storage, hooks for custom pool logic, and ERC-6909 claim balances. Same concentrated-liquidity math as V3 with a radically cheaper, more extensible architecture.

proposedTopics.title: DeFi Oracles
proposedTopics.description: How contracts learn off-chain prices safely: Chainlink push feeds, Uniswap TWAPs, and Pyth pull updates, plus the manipulation-resistance decisions that separate a safe price source from a drainable one.

proposedTopics.title: Constant-product market maker (x*y=k)
proposedTopics.description: The core AMM invariant: reserves x and y must satisfy x*y=k, so a fee-free swap of dx in yields dy = y*dx/(x+dx) out, keeping the product constant. Price is the reserve ratio y/x and moves against the trader as the pool depletes — large trades suffer growing price impact because the curve is convex. With Uniswap V2's 0.3% input fee, only 99.7% of dx is used to price output and the reserve product grows after the full input arrives.
proposedTopics.aiContext: Build: implement defi/amm/ConstantProduct.sol from scratch — swap/addLiquidity/removeLiquidity + a getAmountOut using the (amountIn*997*reserveOut)/(reserveIn*1000+amountIn*997) fee formula; Foundry test in test/defi/ConstantProduct.t.sol. Done when: an invariant/fuzz test proves k (reserve0*reserve1) never DECREASES across any sequence of swaps and that removeLiquidity rounds in the pool's favor. Before contract implementation, derive a small numerical model: assets/liabilities, units and rounding direction, conserved quantities, price/time assumptions, who bears losses, and one stressed or changed case. Record the failing case and compare it with the contract test; an API walkthrough alone does not finish this lesson.

requirements.purpose: Derive the constant-product output and distinguish pricing input from reserve growth after fees

proposedTopics.title: Constant-sum & hybrid AMMs
proposedTopics.description: A constant-sum curve x+y=k gives zero price impact and a fixed 1:1 price but can be fully drained of one asset, so it is unusable alone. StableSwap interpolates between constant-sum near a balanced peg and constant-product as reserves become imbalanced. Understanding both extremes is the setup for its invariant.
proposedTopics.aiContext: Build: in defi/amm/ConstantSum.sol implement x+y=k swaps, then write test/defi/ConstantSum.t.sol proving one asset can be drained to zero; document in a comment why a pure constant-sum pool is arbitrageable to empty. Done when: a test drains reserveY to 0 with a single large swap, demonstrating the failure mode.

requirements.purpose: Compare the constant-sum and constant-product boundary behaviors that StableSwap combines

options.title: StableSwap Whitepaper
options.why: Curve's primary paper defines the constant-sum and constant-product extremes and motivates interpolation for correlated assets.

proposedTopics.title: Stableswap invariant & amplification (Curve)
proposedTopics.description: Curve's StableSwap blends constant-sum and constant-product with an amplification coefficient A: higher A keeps prices near 1:1 across a wider balanced region. With S=Σxᵢ and P=Πxᵢ, its invariant is A*n^n*S + D = A*n^n*D + D^(n+1)/(n^n*P); implementations solve iteratively for D and the output balance. The assumption is correlated assets — a depeg lets arbitrageurs exchange the impaired asset through the flat region.
proposedTopics.aiContext: Build: in defi/amm/StableSwap.sol implement the 2-asset stableswap invariant with a fixed A, solving for D and for get_dy via Newton iteration; test/defi/StableSwap.t.sol compares its slippage to x*y=k. Done when: a test shows near-zero slippage for balanced swaps at high A and that raising A flattens the price curve near the peg.

proposedTopics.title: LP shares & impermanent loss
proposedTopics.description: Liquidity providers deposit both assets and receive fungible LP tokens representing a pro-rata claim on the reserves. Because a constant-product pool is arbitraged to the external price, an LP ends up with more of the relatively cheaper asset. Impermanent loss is the pool-versus-hold value gap before fees; for an initially balanced, fee-free position it depends on the ending price ratio, while path-dependent fees can offset it.
proposedTopics.aiContext: Build: in defi/amm/LiquidityMath.sol add a pure function computing IL as a function of the price ratio r (IL = 2*sqrt(r)/(1+r) - 1) and test it against hand-worked cases (r=2 -> ~5.7% loss, r=4 -> 20%). Done when: test/defi/LiquidityMath.t.sol matches the closed-form IL at r=1,2,4 within rounding. Before contract implementation, derive a small numerical model: assets/liabilities, units and rounding direction, conserved quantities, price/time assumptions, who bears losses, and one stressed or changed case. Record the failing case and compare it with the contract test; an API walkthrough alone does not finish this lesson.

proposedTopics.title: Uniswap V2 pair & reserves
proposedTopics.description: Each pair holds reserve0/reserve1 of two sorted tokens and enforces x*y=k in swap(): it optimistically sends the requested outputs, then requires the post-balances adjusted for the 0.3% fee (balance*1000 - amountIn*3) to satisfy the scaled invariant. The factory deploys one pair per sorted token pair with CREATE2, so its address is derivable from factory, salt, and init-code hash. sync() updates reserves to balances; skim() transfers only balance excess without changing reserves.

Done when: swap reverts if the caller doesn't pay enough input to keep k*1000^2 non-decreasing, and the factory's computed CREATE2 address matches the deployed pair.

proposedTopics.title: Uniswap V2 LP mint/burn math
proposedTopics.description: The first liquidity provider mints sqrt(amount0*amount1) - MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY shares, while MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY (1000 units) is permanently locked at address(0), increasing the cost of share-value inflation. Later deposits mint min(amount0*totalSupply/reserve0, amount1*totalSupply/reserve1); integer division rounds down, and depositing an unmatched excess does not increase shares.
proposedTopics.aiContext: Build: implement mint()/burn() in defi/univ2/Pair.sol with the sqrt-minus-MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY first mint and the min() subsequent mint; test/defi/Univ2Mint.t.sol. Done when: a fuzz test shows the second depositor can never mint more shares than their pro-rata contribution and that donating extra of one token does not increase minted shares.

proposedTopics.title: Uniswap V2 TWAP oracle
proposedTopics.description: The pair accumulates price0CumulativeLast += price0*timeElapsed, with price0 encoded as the UQ112.112 ratio reserve1/reserve0. _update records the previous reserves' price before replacing them, at most once per block because timeElapsed is then zero. A consumer differences two cumulative snapshots and divides by elapsed time; if no pair write occurs at the endpoint, it must first extend the cumulative counterfactually from the current reserves. Manipulating a longer average requires sustaining distortion across time, but short windows and thin liquidity remain weak.
proposedTopics.aiContext: Build: in defi/oracle/Univ2Twap.sol compute the time-weighted average from two cumulative snapshots, extending the endpoint cumulative from the current reserves when no pair write occurred; test/defi/Univ2Twap.t.sol uses vm.warp to advance blocks. Done when: an idle endpoint still produces the manually accumulated TWAP within fixed-point rounding, and a single-block spike barely moves a long-window average.

proposedTopics.title: Uniswap V2 flash swaps
proposedTopics.description: swap() sends output before checking the invariant and calls uniswapV2Call when data is non-empty, so the recipient can use the assets before paying within the same transaction. The final balance-adjusted invariant enforces payment in either token. Returning the same token requires amountReturned >= ceil(amountOut*1000/997), an effective fee of about 0.3009% of the withdrawn amount, not merely amountOut plus 0.3%.

proposedTopics.title: Uniswap V2 protocol fee (1/6)
proposedTopics.description: When feeTo is enabled, _mintFee lazily mints protocol LP shares during the next mint or burn. The target is one-sixth of fee-driven liquidity growth: liquidity = totalSupply*(sqrt(k)-sqrt(kLast))/(5*sqrt(k)+sqrt(kLast)). kLast is updated after liquidity events while fees are on and cleared when they are turned off; the protocol does not skim tokens on each swap.

proposedTopics.title: Concentrated liquidity & the L parameter
proposedTopics.description: V3 lets an LP concentrate liquidity L within [pa,pb]. In range, amount0 = L*(sqrt(pb)-sqrt(P))/(sqrt(P)*sqrt(pb)) and amount1 = L*(sqrt(P)-sqrt(pa)); below the range it is all token0, and above it is all token1. Concentration provides greater depth in-range, but a position earns swap fees only while its liquidity is active.

proposedTopics.title: Ticks & tick spacing
proposedTopics.description: V3 maps tick i to price 1.0001^i. Position bounds must be divisible by the pool's immutable tickSpacing; the factory initially enabled fee/spacing pairs 0.05%/10, 0.3%/60, and 1%/200, and later governance can enable more (including 0.01%/1). Crossing an initialized tick applies its signed liquidityNet so positions enter or leave the active-liquidity set.

Done when: round-tripping tick -> sqrtPriceX96 -> tick is stable wherever the inverse accepts the ratio, MAX_SQRT_RATIO is rejected as the exclusive upper bound, and spacing-snapping rejects mis-aligned ticks.

proposedTopics.title: sqrtPriceX96 & Q64.96 fixed point
proposedTopics.description: V3 stores sqrt(token1/token0) as Q64.96: sqrtPriceX96 = floor(sqrt(price)*2^96), so the raw price is (sqrtPriceX96/2^96)^2 before token-decimal adjustment. SqrtPriceMath advances this value with direction-specific formulas and deliberate rounding; blindly converting through floating point or ignoring token ordering and decimals breaks integrations.
proposedTopics.aiContext: Build: in defi/univ3/PriceMath.sol implement priceToSqrtPriceX96 and back, and a getNextSqrtPrice for a given input amount along a tick; test/defi/PriceMath.t.sol. Done when: converting a human price to sqrtPriceX96 and back is lossless to rounding, and a swap step's next sqrt price matches the reference SqrtPriceMath output.

proposedTopics.title: Uniswap V3 fee growth & positions
proposedTopics.description: V3 tracks feeGrowthGlobal0/1X128 per unit of active liquidity. Tick.getFeeGrowthInside conditionally derives growth below and above each boundary from feeGrowthOutside, then subtracts both from global growth. A position snapshots inside growth and accrues liquidity*(insideNow-insideLast)/2^128 with modular-overflow semantics. Distinct ranges and snapshots make positions non-fungible at the periphery layer.

Done when: a position accrues fees only for swaps that occur while the price sits inside its range, and zero while price is outside.

proposedTopics.title: Uniswap V4 flash accounting (lock/unlock)
proposedTopics.description: State-changing V4 pool operations run after PoolManager.unlock calls the caller's unlockCallback. Operations accrue signed per-caller currency deltas in transient storage; unlock reverts unless the count of nonzero deltas returns to zero. settle pays a negative delta and take withdraws a positive one, so a route can settle net currency movement rather than transfer at every hop.
proposedTopics.aiContext: Build: in defi/univ4/Router.sol implement an unlockCallback that swaps across two pools and settles all currency deltas to zero; test/defi/FlashAccounting.t.sol. Done when: a route that leaves any non-zero delta reverts on unlock, while a correctly settled route pays and withdraws only its net currency deltas.

proposedTopics.title: Uniswap V4 hooks
proposedTopics.description: A V4 hook is a contract called at selected pool lifecycle points. Hooks.sol derives enabled callbacks from the least-significant bits of the hook address, so CREATE2 salt mining is commonly used to obtain a matching address. A beforeSwap hook can return a fee override only for a dynamic-fee pool and must set the override flag; hook code can alter or block execution, so its trust model is part of pool risk.

Done when: the override changes the swap fee, omitting the override flag does not, and PoolManager rejects a hook address whose permission bits are invalid.

proposedTopics.title: Uniswap V3 TWAP from tick cumulatives
proposedTopics.description: V3 observations store tickCumulative and secondsPerLiquidityCumulativeX128 in a ring. observe([window,0]) returns past and current cumulatives; dividing their tick-cumulative difference by window yields the arithmetic mean tick, with negative division rounded toward negative infinity before quote conversion. increaseObservationCardinalityNext expands capacity only as later observations are written. proposedTopics.title: Pyth pull oracle
proposedTopics.description: Pyth's EVM pull integration has the application submit updateData, pay getUpdateFee, call updatePriceFeeds, then read getPriceNoOlderThan(id,maxAge). Price and conf share expo, so values are integer*10^expo. The age bound is explicit and a wide confidence interval can require conservative pricing or rejection. Pyth also offers push integration, so 'pull' describes this integration path rather than every Pyth feed.
proposedTopics.aiContext: Build: in defi/oracle/PythConsumer.sol update then read a price with getPriceNoOlderThan, reject a nonpositive price, apply expo, and reject if conf/abs(price) exceeds a tolerance; test/defi/PythConsumer.t.sol with a mock Pyth. Done when: reading without a fresh update reverts on max-age, nonpositive prices revert, and a wide confidence interval is rejected by the tolerance check. Version check 2026-09-25: the official August 26, 2026 upgrade guide states Hermes now requires a Pyth API key (https://docs.pyth.network/price-feeds/core/upgrade/preparing). Keep the deterministic mock lab; for live integration check current contract/feed IDs and SDK compatibility, keep service credentials out of shared artifacts, and test missing/failed Hermes authentication separately from stale on-chain prices.

proposedTopics.title: Oracle manipulation resistance
proposedTopics.description: Oracle safety depends on the source, liquidity, averaging window, update model, staleness policy, and value at risk. A same-transaction AMM spot read is manipulable because the attacker can trade before use and reverse afterward. TWAPs increase the cost of sustaining distortion but do not guarantee safety; external feeds introduce different liveness and configuration risks. Cross-checks need explicit divergence and failure policies rather than blind averaging.

proposedPrompts.promptText: For a constant-product pool with reserves x, y and a fee-free input dx, derive the output dy and explain why large trades slip.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Keep x*y=k: after adding fee-free dx, x'=x+dx, so y'=k/x' and dy=y-y'=y*dx/(x+dx). The marginal price moves continuously against a larger trade on the convex curve. With Uniswap V2's fee, getAmountOut prices as though 997/1000 of input entered, but the pair receives the full input; its adjusted-balance check therefore permits and normally produces reserve-product growth. Pitfall: confusing the priced input with the final token balance gives the wrong invariant explanation.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write Uniswap's getAmountOut with the 0.3% fee baked in.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: function getAmountOut(uint amountIn, uint rIn, uint rOut) pure returns (uint) { uint inWithFee = amountIn * 997; uint num = inWithFee * rOut; uint den = rIn * 1000 + inWithFee; return num / den; } // fee taken from input, division truncates in the pool's favor

proposedPrompts.promptText: Ethernaut level 22 (Dex): drain almost all of one token from the two-token AMM.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: The Dex prices swaps as amount*toReserve/fromReserve with integer truncation and no invariant guard; swap the full balance back and forth so the ratio skews further each round until one side rounds enough in your favor to take nearly the entire reserve. It shows why a naive spot-price AMM without a k check is drainable.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Why is a pure constant-sum (x+y=k) pool unusable on its own, and what does a hybrid curve fix?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: x+y=k gives a fixed 1:1 price and zero price impact, so an arbitrageur can swap until one reserve hits zero — there is no rising marginal price to stop them. StableSwap approximates constant-sum near balance but bends toward constant-product as reserves skew. Pitfall: the flat region assumes correlated assets; after a depeg it lets arbitrageurs exchange the impaired asset for the good one cheaply.

proposedPrompts.promptText: What does the amplification coefficient A control in Curve's stableswap, and what is its hidden risk?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: A interpolates between constant-sum (high A: prices pinned near 1:1 across a wide balance range, great for pegged pairs) and constant-product (low A: more slippage but reserves never exhaust). The invariant has no closed form, so D and outputs are solved by on-chain Newton iteration. Pitfall: high A assumes the peg holds — if an asset depegs, the flat low-slippage region becomes a trap where arbitrage drains the good asset cheaply, exactly what happened in stablecoin depeg events.

proposedPrompts.promptText: What is impermanent loss, and on what does it actually depend?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: It is the shortfall between holding LP position value and just holding the two tokens, caused by the pool auto-rebalancing along x*y=k so you end up heavier in the asset that dropped. It depends on the RATIO of price change, not volatility alone: IL = 2*sqrt(r)/(1+r) - 1 where r is the price ratio (r=2 -> ~5.7%, r=4 -> ~20%). Pitfall: it is only 'impermanent' if price returns; if you withdraw after a permanent move, the loss is realized and only offset if accrued fees exceeded it.

proposedPrompts.promptText: How does Uniswap V2's swap() enforce the invariant and the fee without computing an output amount itself?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: It optimistically transfers the caller-requested outputs, infers input from post-callback balances, then requires (balance0*1000-amount0In*3)*(balance1*1000-amount1In*3) >= reserve0*reserve1*1000^2. Underpayment reverts. Reserves are cached: sync() sets reserves to current balances, while skim() transfers only balance excess and leaves reserves unchanged. Pitfall: treating skim and sync as equivalent reconciliation operations reverses their intended effects.

proposedPrompts.promptText: How many LP shares does the first vs a subsequent depositor mint in Uniswap V2, and why the MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY burn?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: First: sqrt(amount0*amount1) - MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY, with 1000 raw share units permanently sent to address(0). Subsequent: min(amount0*totalSupply/reserve0, amount1*totalSupply/reserve1), so only the limiting side is credited and division rounds down. Locking the initial 1000 shares raises the cost of donation-driven share-value inflation; it is not a universal proof against every vault inflation path. Pitfall: an imbalanced deposit gifts the uncredited excess to existing LPs.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write the subsequent-deposit LP mint amount for Uniswap V2.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: uint liquidity = Math.min(amount0 * totalSupply / reserve0, amount1 * totalSupply / reserve1); // MIN over both assets, integer division rounds down (pool-favorable); the excess of the over-supplied token is not credited

proposedPrompts.promptText: How is a Uniswap V2 TWAP computed, and what makes it manipulation-resistant (and where does it still fail)?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: The pair accumulates price*timeElapsed into priceCumulativeLast (UQ112.112) before reserves change; a consumer takes (cumulative_t2-cumulative_t1)/(t2-t1). If no pair write occurs at t2, extend the cumulative counterfactually from current reserves or the endpoint is stale. Sustaining distortion across time is costlier than an atomic spot move, but thin liquidity or a short window remains weak. Pitfall: stored cumulative values do not advance merely because time passes.

proposedPrompts.promptText: What makes a Uniswap V2 flash swap possible, and what enforces repayment?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: swap() sends output before its adjusted-k check and calls uniswapV2Call when data is non-empty, so the recipient can act before payment. Returning the same token requires returned >= ceil(amountOut*1000/997), about 0.3009% of amountOut; payment in the other token is also allowed if the final invariant passes. Pitfall: amountOut plus 0.3% can underpay because the fee is charged on input and integer repayment must round up.

proposedPrompts.promptText: How does Uniswap V2 collect its 1/6 protocol fee, and why lazily via sqrt(k)?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: When feeTo is on, the protocol targets one-sixth of the 30-bp LP fee (5 bp) by minting shares on the next mint/burn: liquidity = totalSupply*(sqrt(k)-sqrt(kLast))/(5*sqrt(k)+sqrt(kLast)). Measuring sqrt(k) growth avoids per-swap accounting. kLast is refreshed after liquidity events while fees are on; if fees are off and kLast is nonzero, _mintFee clears it. Pitfall: it mints LP shares rather than transferring reserve tokens per swap.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write the conversions between a price and sqrtPriceX96 (Q64.96).
proposedPrompts.answerHint: // price1e18 is token1/token0 scaled by 1e18; this compact forward form has an explicit shift bound\nfunction priceToSqrtX96(uint price1e18) pure returns (uint160) { require(price1e18 <= type(uint64).max); return uint160(Math.sqrt(price1e18 << 192) / 1e9); }\nfunction sqrtX96ToPrice1e18(uint160 s) pure returns (uint) { uint q96 = 1 << 96; return FullMath.mulDiv(FullMath.mulDiv(s, s, q96), 1e18, q96); } // same 1e18 scale; use a 512-bit sqrt design when the bound is too narrow

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write getAmount1 for a Uniswap V3 position (amount of token1 for liquidity L over a sqrt-price range).
proposedPrompts.answerHint: // amount1 = L * (sqrtP - sqrtPa), clamped so sqrtP stays within [sqrtPa, sqrtPb]\nfunction getAmount1(uint128 L, uint160 sqrtA, uint160 sqrtB, uint160 sqrtP) pure returns (uint) { if (sqrtP < sqrtA) sqrtP = sqrtA; if (sqrtP > sqrtB) sqrtP = sqrtB; return uint(L) * (sqrtP - sqrtA) / (1 << 96); }

proposedPrompts.promptText: In Uniswap V3, what does liquidity L represent and what happens when price leaves a position's range?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: L is the concentrated liquidity active within [pa, pb]; inside the range the position holds amount0 = L*(sqrt(pb)-sqrt(P))/(sqrt(P)*sqrt(pb)) and amount1 = L*(sqrt(P)-sqrt(pa)), acting like a constant-product pool with virtual reserves so the same capital gives deeper liquidity near P. Outside the range it is entirely one asset and earns no swap fees until price re-enters. Pitfall: concentration increases in-range capital efficiency while concentrating price exposure; it does not apply one universal multiplier to fee yield or impermanent loss.

proposedPrompts.promptText: What is a tick in Uniswap V3, and why does each fee tier have a tickSpacing?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Tick i maps to price 1.0001^i; a position's bounds must be divisible by that pool's immutable tickSpacing. The factory initially enabled 0.05%/10, 0.3%/60, and 1%/200, and governance later enabled 0.01%/1; more fee/spacing pairs can be enabled, so the list is not a protocol constant. Pitfall: only crossing an initialized tick applies liquidityNet; an aligned but uninitialized tick does not change active liquidity.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Why does Uniswap V3 store sqrt(price) as a Q64.96 number, and how do you convert back to price?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: sqrtPriceX96 = floor(sqrt(price) * 2^96) where price is token1/token0; recover price = (sqrtPriceX96 / 2^96)^2. Tracking sqrt(price) makes each swap step linear in sqrt-price along a tick (no per-step square root), and Q64.96 (64 integer + 96 fractional bits) preserves precision across the whole price range. Pitfall: forgetting the 2^96 scale or flipping the token0/token1 direction inverts or mis-scales the price by huge factors — a very common integration bug.

proposedPrompts.promptText: How does Uniswap V3 attribute fees to a specific position's range?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: It tracks feeGrowthGlobalX128 (fees per unit liquidity, Q128.128) and, per tick, feeGrowthOutside; feeGrowthInside(lower, upper) = global - outside(lower) - outside(upper) (adjusted by which side the current tick is on). Owed fees = liquidity * (feeGrowthInside_now - feeGrowthInside_last), so only fees earned while price was inside the range count. Pitfall: this per-range accounting is why V3 positions are NFTs — fees aren't a fungible pro-rata claim like V2 LP tokens, and an out-of-range position accrues nothing.

proposedPrompts.promptText: What changes when every Uniswap V4 pool lives inside one singleton PoolManager?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: All pools' tokens are custodied by one contract and pool state is keyed by PoolId, so creating a pool is a cheap state write (not a deployment) and multi-hop swaps net internally instead of transferring tokens between separate pool contracts. The concentrated-liquidity math is identical to V3; the gain is architectural — shared custody plus flash accounting cuts gas sharply. Pitfall: a single custody contract concentrates risk, so V4's core is heavily audited and hooks (not the manager) carry the customizable — and riskier — logic.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Explain V4's flash accounting: how do lock/unlock and currency deltas guarantee solvency?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Operations run inside PoolManager.unlock(): swaps/liquidity changes accrue signed currency deltas in EIP-1153 transient storage, and unlock reverts unless every delta returns to zero. settle() pays a negative delta and take() withdraws a positive one. Net settlement can avoid intermediate pool-to-pool transfers, but the exact transfer count depends on router behavior. Pitfall: any unsettled non-zero delta reverts the whole transaction.

proposedPrompts.promptText: How does Uniswap V4 know which callbacks a hook implements, and why is that encoded in the address?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: The hook's ADDRESS low bits are permission flags (beforeSwap, afterSwap, before/afterAddLiquidity, etc.); the PoolManager reads those bits to decide which callbacks to invoke, so hooks are CREATE2-mined to an address whose bits match their implemented functions. This makes permissions immutable and gas-cheap to check. Pitfall: a hook is untrusted code the pool calls mid-operation — a malicious or buggy hook can tax, block, or reorder swaps, so hook trust is part of a pool's risk profile, not an afterthought.

proposedPrompts.promptText: What do ERC-6909 claim tokens let a Uniswap V4 trader avoid, and when does it pay off?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Instead of withdrawing ERC-20s after each action, a trader can hold CLAIM balances (ERC-6909, a minimal multi-token standard without transfer callbacks) inside the PoolManager and settle later swaps from them — pure internal ledger updates, no real token transfers. It pays off for high-frequency traders/MEV bots and routers doing many actions per block. Pitfall: 6909 balances live inside the manager, so they carry the manager's custody risk and must eventually be redeemed to real tokens to leave the system.

proposedPrompts.promptText: What must a Chainlink consumer validate on latestRoundData(), and why is a 'push' feed shaped this way?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Validate answer > 0, reject updatedAt==0 or an age beyond your policy, and normalize using the proxy's decimals() rather than assuming 8. Each feed updates when its configured deviation threshold or heartbeat is met, so retrieve those parameters from the official feed directory and choose an application limit. Pitfall: answer>0 alone accepts a healthy-looking value indefinitely after updates stop.

proposedPrompts.topicTitle: Uniswap V3 TWAP from tick cumulatives
proposedPrompts.promptText: How do you derive a TWAP from a Uniswap V3 pool's observations?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Call observe([window,0]); arithmeticMeanTick=(tickCumulativeNow-tickCumulativePast)/window, correcting a negative non-exact quotient down by one because Solidity division truncates toward zero. Quote at that tick to obtain the geometric-mean price. increaseObservationCardinalityNext only schedules capacity that subsequent writes populate; requesting older-than-initialized history reverts OLD. Pitfall: capacity, initialized history, liquidity, and window length all matter to safety.

proposedPrompts.promptText: How does a Pyth pull oracle differ from a Chainlink push feed in the consumer's flow?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: In Pyth's EVM pull integration, submit updateData, pay getUpdateFee to updatePriceFeeds, then call getPriceNoOlderThan(id,maxAge). Price and conf both scale by 10^expo, so compare conf/abs(price) without losing precision. Unlike this caller-submitted path, push integrations update independently. Pitfall: Pyth supports both pull and push; regardless of path, enforce freshness and a protocol-specific confidence policy.

proposedPrompts.promptText: What is the single question that decides whether a price source is safe to trust for collateral?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Manipulation cost relative to value at risk is necessary, not sufficient. Also model source independence, market liquidity, averaging duration, update and liveness behavior, freshness, divergence handling, and failure policy. An atomic AMM spot read is weak because an attacker can move and reverse it in one transaction while paying trading costs; a TWAP raises the cost by requiring distortion over time but is not absolute protection. Pitfall: decentralization alone says nothing about manipulation resistance.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Damn Vulnerable DeFi — Puppet: drain the lending pool that prices collateral from a Uniswap spot pool.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: The lending pool computes required collateral from a manipulable Uniswap spot price; sell enough token into the AMM to crater that quote, then borrow against the artificially cheap valuation. Puppet variants change the AMM and collateral mechanics but preserve the same unsafe spot-oracle root. The fix is a manipulation-resistant oracle and explicit risk bounds, not merely blocking flash loans.
